objective: Genuine evidence-based engagement on third-party food-science posts, not engagement spam

drafts.topic_condition: Post explains food safety controls, food technology or HACCP
drafts.comment: What makes food safety education valuable is connecting the science behind a control with its practical use. Explaining why a step matters can be just as important as explaining how to perform it.

drafts.topic_condition: Post explains a new study or food-processing technology
drafts.comment: A fascinating direction for food science communication is showing both the practical application and the limits of the evidence. That context helps readers distinguish promising research from established practice.

drafts.topic_condition: Post concerns allergens, food labels or food recalls
drafts.comment: Food safety messages work best when consumers can turn them into clear, practical decisions. Explaining the difference between a precaution, a legal requirement and a verified risk is especially helpful.

drafts.topic_condition: Post explains a nutrition or food-science study
drafts.comment: Making research accessible without losing scientific nuance is so important. Study design and limitations deserve a place in short-form explanations too, not just the headline conclusion.

drafts.topic_condition: Post discusses food microbiology or foodborne pathogens
drafts.comment: Food microbiology is a great example of why translating research into clear everyday language matters. A short explanation of the methods and uncertainty can make these findings much easier to interpret responsibly.
